title: Trapped Rainwater
statement:
Compute how much rain a row of bars can hold after a storm.

Contract
- `heights` is a non-null array of non-negative `int` values; each entry is the height of a bar one unit wide, and bars touch each other.
- Water collects above a bar up to the lower of the tallest bar to its left and the tallest bar to its right (both including the bar itself); water above the edges of the row runs off.
- Return the total water volume over all bars as a `long`, since it can exceed the `int` range.
- The array may be empty or have fewer than three bars, which hold nothing. Do not mutate `heights`.

Examples
- `trap(new int[]{0, 2, 0, 3, 1, 0, 2})` returns `5`: 2 above the second 0, 1 above the 1 and 2 above the last 0.
- `trap(new int[]{3, 1, 3})` returns `2`.
- `trap(new int[]{1, 2, 3})` returns `0`, because a staircase drains away.
hints: Look at one bar at a time: the water above it depends only on the tallest bars on each side.
Precomputing the tallest bar to the left and to the right of every position gives a simple linear solution with extra arrays.

To drop the arrays, move two pointers inward and always advance the side whose running maximum is smaller, since that side's water level is already known. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the number of bars.
inputSyntax: Input: the bar heights, for example: [0, 2, 0, 3, 1, 0, 2]
